named-arguments.comment: Kotlin named arguments (state = ..., onLike = ..., modifier = ...) get no scope at all, which is why Compose reads so pale next to Flutter. Dart's equivalent is variable.parameter.named.dart. Two forms: the name alone on its line, and the name right after ( or , on one line.

property-access.comment: Kotlin leaves the segments of a property chain unscoped, same as Dart does. Method calls are excluded - they are followed by '(' and already scoped entity.name.function.call.kotlin.

object-reference.comment: The head of a property chain (MaterialTheme.shapes, TextOverflow.Ellipsis, Alignment.CenterVertically) is left unscoped by the Kotlin grammar. Kotlin convention capitalises objects and types, so a capitalised identifier directly before a dot is a type/object reference - Flutter's equivalent is support.class.dart.
